text:
Like an angel seated in a barber's hands,

I live, raising the deeply ribbed tankard,

hypogastrium and neck bowed, with my pipe,

under a swollen wind of light veils.


Like warm droppings from old dovecotes,

a thousand Dreams give me gentle burnings


and my sad heart resembles the sapwood

bloodied by the ocher golds the tree weeps.


Then, after carefully swallowing my Dreams,

I turn and, after drinking thirty or forty tankards,

I collect myself, releasing my fierce urgencies:


meek as the Lord of cedar and hyssop,

I piss toward the brown sky, high, high, so far...

with the consent of the heliotropes.

translation.title: Evening Prayer
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves Rimbaud's grotesque parody of prayer, mixing sacred diction with bodily irreverence.
